title: Floorplan: k8s topology templates + failsafe install patterns (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects compact, reusable topology templates and 'failsafe' installation patterns for on-prem Kubernetes clusters we commonly ship: single-rack small installations, multi-rack HA deployments, and vSphere converged setups. It focuses on the physical / VM floorplan, the minimum Terraform module mapping required to express the topology, and a short ops playbook for bootstrap, rollout, upgrade and emergency rollback recovery.

Scope and assumptions:
- Audience: platform engineers and field SREs preparing private deployments for customers.
- Intended to be vendor-agnostic where possible, but includes pragmatic vSphere and IPMI/BMC guidance.
- Assumes access to a private network with DHCP / IPAM or static assignment, a reachable BMC/IPMI management plane, and a storage option (local NVMe, external SAN, or Ceph/Longhorn).
- We target kubeadm-based bootstraps (explicit kubeadm steps) because of predictable control-plane lifecycle and offline-friendly operation. Patterns apply to k0s/k3s adaptations but are out of scope for exact commands.

1) Topology templates (high level)
A. Small single-rack dev/test (3 control-plane tolerant, 6 workers)
- Rack: 1 RU switches, 3 master nodes (dual-NIC: mgmt + data), 6 worker nodes.
- Storage: local NVMe on workers for ephemeral workloads, NFS for shared legacy storage.
- Networking: VLANs for management (BMC), control-plane, pod network, and storage.
- BMC/IPMI: VLANed mgmt network with jump-box bastion for BMC access.
- Terraform mapping: hardware_group { name = "rackA"; count_cp = 3; count_worker = 6; bmc_pool = "rackA-bmc" }

B. Multi-rack HA (2+ racks, 5 control-plane via 3+2 distribution, 24+ workers)
- Rack distribution: spread control-plane across racks for fault domain isolation (ex: CP nodes in racks A, B and backup CP nodes in rack C).
- Storage: Ceph/ROOK or external SAN with iSCSI/Ceph CSI for resilient PVs.
- Load balancer: external VIP via F5/HAProxy/MetalLB with ARP/VRRP.
- Terraform mapping: hardware_group per-rack and a platform overlay for storage and LB: hardware_group { name = "rackA"; az = "rackA" } + storage_module { type = "ceph" }

C. vSphere converged (VM-first template for customers that prefer virtualization)
- vSphere resource pools: create dedicated folders and resource pools for control-plane and workers.
- VM sizing recommendations: CP: 8vCPU/32GB with 100GB disk; Worker: 16vCPU/128GB for GPU nodes or 8vCPU/32GB for general purpose.
- Terraform mapping: vsphere_vm module per-role with templates (golden images configured with containerd + cloud-init).
- Networking: use dvSwitch with dvPortGroup per VLAN; ensure MTU consistent for CNI.

2) Terraform module notes (practical details)
- Module layout suggestion (flat):
  - modules/hardware_group/main.tf (provisions chassis/VMs, BMC objects)
  - modules/lb/main.tf (metalLB / external LB registration)
  - modules/storage/main.tf (creates Ceph pools or attaches iSCSI extents)
  - modules/network/main.tf (VLANs, subnet, IPAM leases)
- Important variables to expose:
  - hardware_group.name (string)
  - hardware_group.bmc_prefix (string) // used for BMC templates
  - hardware_group.control_plane_count (number)
  - hardware_group.worker_count (number)
  - platform.storage_type ("local" | "ceph" | "iscsi")
  - platform.lb_mode ("metal" | "external")
- Safe apply patterns:
  - Always run terraform plan with -out=plan.tfplan; commit plan artifact to CI for review.
  - Block apply inside maintenance windows unless it's a canary change to a single rack.
  - Use resource targeting only for non-infra-impacting changes; avoid targeting control-plane VMs unless ephemeral.

3) Bootstrap playbook (kubeadm-based, minimal commands)
- Prep (preflight):
  - Ensure BMC access: test ipmi/ipmitool lan print and remote power control.
  - Confirm DNS / NTP across nodes; pre-seed /etc/hosts if necessary for offline installs.
  - Images: preload containerd images on hosts or ensure internal registry mirror exists.
- Steps:
  1) Provision hardware/VMs via Terraform and tag with role=control-plane/worker.
  2) On CP nodes, install containerd, kubeadm, kubelet, kubectl pinned to target version.
  3) Initialize first control-plane: kubeadm init --config kubeadm-config.yaml --upload-certs
  4) Join additional control-planes with kubeadm join --control-plane --certificate-key <key>
  5) Install CNI after control-plane up (we prefer calico or cilium depending on MTU/ENV).
  6) Join worker nodes with kubeadm join <args>.
  7) Install storage CSI (Longhorn/ROOK) only after cluster steady-state and node labeling.

4) Failsafe patterns and preflight checklist (short)
- Secrets: never store raw BMC creds in the Terraform state; use vault or KMS-wrapped variables.
- Boot order safety: when provisioning PXE/IPXE images, ensure fallback images are available and a manual rescue target in BMC.
- Graceful node replacement: for baremetal with typed disks, have a documented disk-wipe image and a local boot mode that preserves ID labels for re-attachable volumes.
- Control-plane protection: keep a minimum of 3 CP nodes online; if you must take >1 down, re-elect a temporary leader via kubeadm.

5) Upgrade plan (minor & major)
- Pre-upgrade: run kubeconformance + smoke tests in a staging environment with identical topology template. Take etcd snapshot and push to artifact storage (s3 or internal NFS).
- Minor upgrades (patch/minor):
  1) Upgrade control-plane nodes one at a time: drain, upgrade kubeadm/kubelet, kubeadm upgrade apply, uncordon.
  2) Verify control-plane health (kubectl get cs, etcd endpoint health).
  3) Rolling upgrade workers in small batches (10–20% of fleet) with pod disruption budgets honored.
- Major upgrades (kubeadm model bumps):
  - Follow kubeadm recommended sequence. Use canary rack approach: pick one rack, upgrade CP and workers there and run full regression suite for 24h before wider rollout.

6) Emergency rollback & recovery steps (concise)
- If control-plane fails during upgrade: revert DNS/LB to a previous HAProxy node, restore etcd snapshot to a freshly provisioned CP set (use identical certs if possible).
- Lost a majority of CP: restore etcd from snapshot onto a new 3-node control-plane cluster. Steps: provision VMs -> install kubeadm/kubelet -> restore etcd per docs -> kubeadm init with --config restore-config.yaml.
- Worker failure mass-outage: cordon & drain unaffected workers, scale up node replacements in parallel, reattach external PVs by matching PV nodeAffinity or rebind after manual PV editing.

7) Validation and smoke tests
- Post-provision smoke checks (automatable):
  - kubectl get nodes (all Ready)
  - kube-system pods all Running
  - coredns responds
  - example deploy with service + Ingress through LB
  - pv/pvc lifecycle test for storage backend
- Canary traffic: route a small percentage to new cluster via LB rules for 1–2 hours and check latency/errors.

8) Observability & telemetry hooks for private installs
- Install node-exporter, kube-state-metrics, and prometheus with alerting rules for disk pressure, kubelet crashes, etc.
- Ship metrics to central telemetry only if customer agrees; fallback: local long-term retention via Thanos sidecar + periodic snapshot transfer.

9) Field notes & open questions (WIP)
- Consider a "maintenance mode" tag in terraform to limit autoscaler activity during bootstrap.
- Investigate asset tagging integration with inventory (Ralph/NetBox) for two-way reconciliation.
- Question: do we want a default BMC jump-host image with preinstalled tools (ipmitool, racadm, baseline netcat) or rely on operator laptops? Recommendation: ship jump-host image.

Appendix: Useful command snippets
- etcd snapshot (example):
  ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \n    --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \n    --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.crt \n    --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.key snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db

- kubeadm join worker (example):
  kubeadm join 10.0.0.10:6443 --token <token> --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:<hash>

- terraform safe plan/apply pattern (CI):
  terraform init && terraform plan -out plan.tfplan && terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json && ci-validate plan.json && terraform apply plan.tfplan

If you use this doc in field runbooks, please update the hardware_group variable samples in modules/hardware_group/README.md and attach site-specific floorplans. This is intentionally compact — add environment-specific notes (power-PDU maps, serial console endpoints, and rack mount diagrams) per customer in the site folder.
